findings.text: blocking: the paragraph this delta adds asserts that tests/test_ledger.py::test_every_read_view_returns_and_large_defaults_are_compact 'is killed the same way at the base revision', and the manifest's failure_attribution cites coordinator-base-arm.log for the same claim ('the gate's base arm (coordinator-base-arm.log) fails it at 300s'). That log ran the file and reports '1 failed, 109 passed, 1 error in 380.46s' with the failure being the roadmap.py window bound and the error the new test file's collection, so the ledger case passed there; no log in the run directory shows a base-revision kill of it (grep -l -i timeout over the run's *.log matches only the head-side coordinator-head-arm.log, gate-four-file-final.log and gate-plan-coordinator.log). The byte-identity of tests/test_ledger.py and reckon/ledger.py between 017b346cb4 and 4fed6ea, which the same sentence cites and which I confirmed with git diff --stat, does support 'this change cannot reach it' - but it does not support 'killed the same way', and it is the sentence that turns a red gate into an environmental one for a reader deciding whether to promote. Rest the classification on byte-identity and on the serial-versus-parallel difference, or run a serial base arm and cite it.

non-blocking: the sentence describing the gate log states the log's 'third [line] names the literal command and the module path as imported'. gate-four-file-final.log carries four header lines - '# revision:', '# tree:', '# command:', '# started:' - and no module-as-imported line at all (grep for '__file__' or 'module:' over it returns nothing), so the claim about the artefact is not true of it; the sibling base arm does emit a '# reckon as used:' line, which the clause reads as if the gate log had too. The clause was carried over from the paragraph this delta replaced, so the wording is not new, but the delta rewrote the sentence and kept the inaccuracy.
